A govt functionary said largescale participation of youth gave the campaign, which BJP initially saw as sponsored by AAP and Left-aligned groups, an emotive undercurrent, leaving them little choice but to retreat as the protest grew.For a party which rarely makes any concession to rivals on their terms and exudes an air of bold strength rooted in popular endorsement in polls, BJP’s decision to bow to the student protest also reflects the pragmatism it has shown when confronted with street agitation — better to cut losses than let the pain fester into a more serious challenge.In Nov 2021, Modi had announced withdrawal of farm laws in the face of over a yearlong protest by farmers, which was largely confined to Punjab and parts of Haryana and western UP but had remained stubborn. The PM, too, had ascribed the decision to national interest, which observers thought was a reference to the sensitivity of Punjab as a border state.Pradhan’s mention of the stir at Jantar Mantar but no acknowledgement of Congressled opposition’s protest, which has kept Parliament’s monsoon session deadlocked, is seemingly aimed at denying any credit to BJP’s political rivals while conceding to CJP, which is not really an electoral threat.With Rahul Gandhi, too, stepping up his agitation— his surprise demonstration outside Modi’s residence on July 21 was a highlight — so as not to allow CJP, seen closer to its ‘secular’ rival AAP, hog the limelight, Congress is bound to lay claim to the credit. However, BJP has more often than not seen off its challenge without much political damage.There was sympathy in the ranks for Pradhan who, as petroleum minister, rolled out the vote-spinner Ujjwala scheme and stayed engaged with the cadre. He had a stream of visitors — home minister Amit Shah and finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman included.“We had to swallow the bitter pill because there was a real risk of violence breaking out. Any loss of lives would have been blamed on us. Moreover, it was about students and their families,” said a senior minister.The sense of resignation was accompanied by surprise as to why the leadership did not take measures it subsequently took to tackle the discontent: strengthening of the law against paper leaks, eviction of key bureaucrats from education ministry, drastic action against NTA officials, and Pradhan’s resignation.In his statement, Pradhan, 57, who took charge of education ministry in July 2021, emphasised his decades-long commitment to students and education, and said he took responsibility of the fallout of the NEET-UG paper leak from the very first day.The re-exam result was declared on time, and many poor meritorious students made the cut, he said, while blaming those in responsible positions, alikely swipe at Rahul and other key opposition figures, for trying to mislead students.The BJP brass expressed its full backing for Pradhan, a deft politician who has been the choice of Modi and Shah in helming numerous state elections, as he stepped down. BJP president Nitin Nabin credited him for key reforms and lauded him for prioritising larger interests, in keeping with “the highest standards of integrity and selfless service in public life”.
Article Summary: Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union education minister on Saturday. His ouster marks a political setback to BJP and a rare boost for its rivals. CJP members, led by its founder Abhijeet Dipke, called off their agitation.

Article Title: Govt had to bow before collective struggle of youth, says opposition
Article Text:
Opposition react to Pradhan's exit

NEW DELHI: Following Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, opposition parties Saturday said this marked a victory of democracy and said Modi govt had to "bow before the collective struggle" of the country's youth. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said the youth compelled BJP to bow before their pressure, and also started the countdown to its "ouster from power". "The issue is not limited to one minister or one exam, but reflects a larger breakdown of trust among job aspirants who spend years preparing for competitive exams," he said, calling for strict accountability.NCP-SP chief Sharad Pawar said the resignation was a major victory for youth power.Earlier this week, he met the protesting youths at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. He also met PM Modi a day after."I personally met the PM and told him that dialogue was essential in democracy. If dialogue does not take place, it leads to adverse consequences. I urged the PM to depute senior colleagues to hold talks. I had also told protesters that they should go ahead with talks if govt shows willingness to discuss their demands," Pawar said."Couple of rounds of talks took place. Some of the demands of youths were accepted, they were pressing for the minister's resignation," he said.TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee said, "People in power must realise that power of the people is greater than any office or authority. One can love their country deeply without having to love govt of the day."While Sena UBT president Uddhav Thackeray said, "A single cockroach made a dictator bow down", MNS chief Raj Thackeray said, "Gen Z has uprooted govt's hair. And brought it down to earth."The development has restored people's faith in democracy by proving that govts must ultimately listen to people's voice, AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal said.
Article Summary: Opposition parties say resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan is a victory of democracy. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said the youth compelled BJP to bow before their pressure. NCP-SP chief Sharad Pawar said the resignation was a major victory for youth power.

Article Title: Left scores win, despite its shrunken presence, through its student organs
Article Text:
When the Left-aligned student groups joined the CJP-led protest, they were drawn into the fold organically, said parties’ functionaries

NEW DELHI: It must qualify as a striking case of maximising one's returns on meagre capital. Disproportionate to its marginal presence in Parliament and anaemic strength on the ground, Left parties successfully leveraged AISA, SFI and AISF, which have active units in Delhi, to pressure govt to give into the demand of getting Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as education minister.In fact, AISA members, president Neha Bora and Manish Kumar and Ameen Amitoj, despite having no prior association with Abhijeet Dipke, sat on a 23-day hunger strike in solidarity with the students.The victory of their student outfits, which made common cause with those sections of Gen Z, who are usually not receptive to their "class warfare" trope, could act as a compensation of sorts for the Left in an electorally bleak season, marked by routs in Kerala and West Bengal.Earlier, in another instance of them successfully using their tactical intelligence, the Left, through its farmers' wings, influenced the protests in Punjab against farm sector reforms laws enacted by Modi govt, which had to junk them.If AISA, SFI and AISF were a vocal presence throughout the protest, their mother outfits CPI(ML), CPM and CPI, in that order, complemented the effort on the ground by goading the opposition to support the CJP-led protests.According to Left functionaries, who have been part of the demonstrations, when the Left-aligned students groups joined the students' protest led by CJP, they were drawn into the fold organically and not perceived as people just jumping in for credit as these students have been raising issues around the flaws in the examination system and the challenges through their unions.All 15 MPs belonging to the Left joined the students to protest the police action against them during the march to Parliament on July 20. They also ensured there was no dilution of the demand for Pradhan's resignation.CPI(ML) general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya agreed that the success of the protests has given the Left a fillip. "This movement has re-energised ongoing struggles across the country for democracy, justice, and the defence of the Constitution." He called upon INDIA bloc to carry the energy, resolve, and democratic spirit of this movement into Parliament and intensify the struggle for affordable and quality education for all.CPM general secretary M A Baby said Pradhan's resignation was the first step. "Congratulations to Abhijeet Dipke and CJP, to SFI, AISF, AISA, and lakhs of students and young people for their courage and determination which has won this historic victory. We demand comprehensive reform: scrap NTA! Take back NEP!" CPM said."It is a rare moment of democratic accountability, achieved not through the goodwill of an arrogant govt, but through the sustained struggle of students and youth across the country. The students' movement has defeated the arrogance of BJP and compelled the Modi-Shah regime to answer for its failures," CPI general secretary D Raja said.
Article Summary: Left parties leveraged AISA, SFI and AISF, which have active units in Delhi. AISA members, despite having no prior association with Abhijeet Dipke, sat on a 23-day hunger strike in solidarity with the students.

Article Title: PM Modi is India's past, protesting youth the country's future, says Rahul
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi said "past can never fight the future”.

NEW DELHI: Asserting that "time has come to remove this govt", Congress 's Rahul Gandhi said PM Narendra Modi is India's past while the protesting youth are the country's future. He added that the "past can never fight the future". Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge called education minister Dharmendra Pradhan 's resignation a "victory of truth and defeat of Modi's stubbornness".Rahul said students' agitation has issued a warning that if BJP-RSS continue to run the govt like their personal fiefdom, they would face a stir 10 times more intense than what is happening now. He accused RSS of hollowing India from inside like termites. He said Pradhan's resignation is a signal to other communities that are being "oppressed" by Modi govt, that fighting the govt is a wise step.Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said, "Force was used against them.But the youth did not bend; govt had to bend." She said she had been wondering for the past 10-12 years, "When will we wake up and realise what is being done to our country?" She said the youth are reclaiming their country.Party MP K C Venugopal said, "A massive salute to millions of students across country who compelled this govt to bow down to their will."Rahul said that Pradhan was a symbol of corruption and destruction of world-class education system, and "it is good that he is gone".
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi said PM Narendra Modi is India's past while the protesting youth are the country's future. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge called education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation a "victory of truth and defeat of Modi's stubbornness"

Article Title: Bill proposes 3-month deadline for HCs to dispose of paper leak appeals
Article Text:
Bid to make investigation and judicial process time-bound

What changes in New Bill

NEW DELHI: Aiming to ensure faster disposal of exam paper leak cases, govt has proposed a three-month deadline for respective high courts to dispose of appeals against orders of special fast-track courts, unlike other cases where no such fixed timeline for deciding appeals exists. This converts an open-ended investigation and judicial process into a time-bound one.According to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill circulated to Lok Sabha MPs Saturday, individuals, service providers and organised gangs involved in paper leaks would face longer jail terms, steeper fines, and time-bound investigation and disposal of trials and appeals.As per the bill, which would be introduced in Lok Sabha Monday, the minimum jail term for offences committed by individuals, as well as directors, senior management personnel or persons in charge of service providers conducting public examinations, has been increased to five years.In cases involving organised crime, the minimum imprisonment has been proposed at seven years from the current provision of five years. In all these cases, the maximum jail term would be 10 years.For speedy investigations, the bill proposes govt may constitute a central investigation agency or a special task force (STF). Where an STF has been constituted, it would carry out the investigation. The bill also seeks to insert a new provision mandating that every investigation be completed within two months.The bill provides for day-to-day proceedings and empowers states to establish special fast-track courts in consultation with the chief justice of the respective HC.It mandates that such trial proceedings shall continue until all witnesses in attendance have been examined. These courts would be required to dispose of cases within three months from the date of filing of the chargesheet. All pending trials will be shifted to the special court, and these must also be disposed of within three months.It proposes that any appeal against an order of a fast-track court shall be heard by a division bench of HC. It proposes that every appeal be filed within 30 days from the date of the fast-track court's order and not after a maximum of 90 days under any circumstances.
Article Summary: Govt proposes a three-month deadline for respective high courts to dispose of appeals against orders of special fast-track courts. This converts an open-ended investigation and judicial process into a time-bound one. Minimum jail term for offences committed by individuals, as well as directors, senior management personnel or persons in charge of service providers has been increased to five years.

Article Title: Amarnath yatra resumes via Batal after rain-forced halt
Article Text:
The pilgrimage resumed Saturday

JAMMU: The annual Amarnath Yatra resumed Saturday from Jammu after a six-day suspension forced by rain-caused disruptions, with a fresh batch of over 6,269 pilgrims leaving for the Kashmir cave shrine.The batch, 18th since the yatra started July 3, was flagged off in a convoy of 223 vehicles. “In view of inclement weather, authorities permitted movement of pilgrims only through Baltal, while the traditional Pahalgam route remains closed as a precaution,” an official said.The yatra was suspended on July 19 after heavy rainfall, landslides and unfavourable weather across J&K disrupted both routes -- Pahalgam in Anantnag district and Baltal in Ganderbal --leading to the 3,880-metre high Amarnath cave shrine.Officials said the pilgrimage resumed after weather conditions improved and traffic was restored on Jammu-Srinagar National Highway, which had been blocked by landslides and shooting stones, particularly in the Udhampur-Ramban stretch.LG Manoj Sinha had flagged off the first batch of Amarnath pilgrims early this month. Multi-layered protection is in place, with all pilgrim convoys escorted by security forces.The 57-day yatra concludes on Aug 28, coinciding with Raksha Bandhan.Meanwhile, Border Roads Organisation (BRO)has restored connectivity in Rajouri, Poonch and Reasi, the Jammu border districts where incessant rains triggered multiple landslides.Working on a war footing under Project Sampark, BRO launched a swift and coordinated response to ensure uninterrupted movement of security forces and essential supplies in the three rain-affected districts.“Working tirelessly under hazardous conditions, BRO teams successfully removed debris, stabilised vulnerable stretches and restored traffic on the affected routes in the shortest possible time,” Jammu-based defence PRO Lt Col Suneel Bartwal said.According to the officer, the timely restoration underscores BRO’s unwavering dedication to maintaining strategic infrastructure in remote and border areas. “While essential connectivity on all roads has been restored, teams remain deployed to repair damages and ensure seamless movement of traffic,” Col Bartwal said.
Article Summary: The yatra was suspended on July 19 after heavy rainfall, landslides and unfavourable weather across J&K. The 57-day yatra concludes on Aug 28, coinciding with Raksha Bandhan. Multi-layered protection is in place, with all pilgrim convoys escorted by security forces.

Article Title: 'Will take legal action': CJP firm on punishing cops who used excessive force
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party leaders on Saturday met Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar after the protest against the NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar was called off following education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and the fulfilment of the remaining demands.While speaking to reporters after the meeting, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said they had made it clear that the party would take legal action against every official who used excessive force against students during the July 20 march."There was no specific agenda for the meeting... The discussion took place in a very cordial atmosphere. Senior officers, including the Special Commissioner of the Delhi Police, were also present.We made it clear to them that we have resolved to take legal action against every police officer and RAF personnel who was seen in videos or photographs using excessive force, and those who directly struck people on the head, causing head and hand injuries," Das said."We will initiate legal proceedings against all such police and RAF personnel very soon. We have also launched a website, and when we begin this legal action, we will not only file complaints but also seek the registration of FIRs.If necessary, we will also approach the courts. When the time comes, we will ensure that those officers who fail to uphold law and order and ensure the safety of the people are sent to jail," he added.Meanwhile, Ashutosh Ranka said the party recognises the "consistent cooperation" of the police."It was a good meeting. We discussed everything that has happened over the past few days. What happened on the 20th was very unfortunate. However, we also recognise that there had been consistent cooperation from the Delhi Police," he said."We acknowledged that as well. We hope this marks the beginning of a new chapter. All our demands have been accepted, including the withdrawal of the FIRs and the assurance that no new FIRs will be filed. All's well that ends well, and we sincerely thank the youth of this country," he added.This comes after the Cockroach Janata Party called off its 36-day agitation following Pradhan's resignation and the government's acceptance of its remaining demands.The CJP declared that it was withdrawing its agitation after the government agreed to all its remaining demands, including compensation for the families of students who allegedly died by suicide following the NEET paper leak and the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters.The announcement came after the third round of talks between the two sides at the Constitution Club of India, where Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh met CJP representatives Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.Addressing a joint press conference with the CJP leadership, Nadda said the government would provide "honourable compensation," in accordance with the rules, to the families of students who died by suicide following the NEET examination controversy and ensure the withdrawal of all FIRs registered against protesters.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party leaders met Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar on Saturday. They made it clear that they would take legal action against every official who used excessive force during the July 20 march. This comes after the party called off its agitation following education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and the government's acceptance of its remaining demands.

Article Title: 'Big win for democracy': Arvind Kejriwal congratulates youth on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Article Text:
Arvind Kejriwal congratulates youth on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Saturday hailed the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan as a decisive triumph over governmental arrogance, calling it a milestone moment for the nation's youth and democratic accountability.The minister's departure follows weeks of widespread agitation and a 26-day hunger strike led by activist Sonam Wangchuk over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak controversy. Addressing the nation on X, Arvind Kejriwal extended his congratulations to the youth and Gen Z activists who led the movement. "Congratulations to the entire country on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. Big win for democracy."In an accompanying video message, Kejriwal emphasised how the protest restored faith in civic action during a period of growing public disillusionment: "Hello everyone.Many, many congratulations to all of you. Heartiest congratulations to the youth and Gen Z of our country.It is a matter of great joy that your struggle bore fruit, and ultimately Dharmendra Pradhan had to resign. This is a huge victory for democracy. In our country, people were losing faith in democracy. People had started feeling that governments don't listen, that the public has to keep crying and begging before governments, pleading for everything while governments never listen.""There was such a massive struggle, and ultimately the arrogance of the government had to bow down--it had to yield before the public. This is a very big moment. It is a victory for democracy," he added.Highlighting the severe emotional toll and tragic suicides associated with recurring exam irregularities, Kejriwal urged the Centre to take immediate steps to overhaul the national examination framework."The government must now understand that you have to listen to the people. This is democracy--democracy is by the people, of the people, for the people. I hope the government fixes the NEET system so that paper leaks stop in this country from now on, and our children don't have to commit suicide anymore. Jai Hind."Echoing similar sentiments, AAP Delhi President Saurabh Bharadwaj praised the student movement for achieving what political opposition could not. "There was a lot of arrogance in the fact that when the Bharatiya Janata Party was in power, resignations didn't happen here...Where major opposition parties failed to break that sense of arrogance, the country's Gen Z, the young generation of this country, succeeded in making the government bow down to their demands. "In his resignation letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Dharmendra Pradhan stated that he stepped down to protect student interests and ensure young aspirants do not become "trapped in a web of confusion.""For more than four decades, I have been associated with students, teachers, and the cause of education reform. I have always believed that a strong, inclusive, and forward-looking education system is the foundation of a strong nation," Pradhan wrote. While the resignation marks a key turning point, student groups and activists continue to demand long-term structural reforms and compensation for affected families
Article Summary: Arvind Kejriwal congratulates youth on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. Education minister's departure follows weeks of widespread agitation and a 26-day hunger strike led by activist Sonam Wangchuk over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak controversy. Kejriwal urges the Centre to take immediate steps to overhaul the national examination framework.

Article Title: Pradhan’s five-year term built operating system for NEP, but exam crisis cast shadow
Article Text:
Dharmendra Pradhan (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Dharmendra Pradhan , who stepped down as Union education minister on Saturday after a five-year tenure, leaves behind an education system more standardised, digitally connected and centrally regulated than the one he inherited — but also questions over examination credibility, institutional autonomy, data privacy and the Centre’s capacity to implement reforms on such a large scale.Pradhan, the longest-serving education minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s cabinet, held the portfolio from July 7, 2021, to July 25, 2026. Until 2024, he was also minister for skill development and entrepreneurship.His tenure was less about announcing a new education policy — the National Education Policy had been approved in 2020 — and more about constructing the machinery required to put it into operation.The defining theme was standardisation and portability: common entrance examinations, transferable academic credits, permanent student identification numbers, comparable assessment standards and an attempted umbrella regulator for higher education.The Common University Entrance Test, introduced in 2022, sought to replace differing Class XII board cut-offs with a common admission platform for central universities.It also dramatically expanded the role of the National Testing Agency, whose functioning and credibility later became one of the biggest challenges of Pradhan’s tenure.The National Credit Framework, Academic Bank of Credits and four-year undergraduate programmes were designed to allow students to accumulate and transfer credits, pursue multidisciplinary courses and enter or leave programmes without losing their academic record.APAAR, envisaged as a permanent academic identity for every student, sought to link school, university and skill qualifications through DigiLocker and the credit bank. While intended to ease mobility, it triggered concerns over consent and protection of children’s data.In school education, the ministry released curriculum frameworks for the foundational stage and school education, operationalising the NEP’s 5+3+3+4 structure. PM SHRI was launched to upgrade more than 14,500 existing government schools as models of NEP implementation, while PARAKH was established to develop common assessment standards and bring greater comparability among school boards.Other big-ticket measures included the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, One Nation One Subscription for access to research journals, PM-USHA funding for state universities, permission for foreign universities to open campuses in India and the establishment of IIT campuses abroad.Pradhan also pushed Indian-language textbooks, multidisciplinary education, vocational integration and apprenticeship programmes, drawing on the overlap between his education and skill-development portfolios.The proposed replacement of UGC, AICTE and NCTE with an umbrella regulatory architecture remained unfinished. Implementation also met resistance from some states over language, curriculum and centrally sponsored schemes.Ultimately, the sharpest contradiction of the Pradhan years lay in national testing. Common examinations were meant to deliver fairness and uniformity, but paper leaks, cancellations and administrative failures raised doubts about whether centralisation had moved faster than institutional capacity.
Article Summary: Pradhan was the longest-serving education minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s cabinet. He held the portfolio from July 7, 2021, to July 25, 2026. His tenure was less about announcing a new education policy and more about constructing machinery required to put it into operation.

Article Title: "Unwavering commitment to ethical values": Delhi CM Rekha Gupta praises Dharmendra Pradhan following resignation
Article Text:
"Unwavering commitment to ethical values": Delhi CM Rekha Gupta praises Dharmendra Pradhan following resignation

माननीय श्री @dpradhanbjp जी ने अपने सार्वजनिक जीवन में हर दायित्व को निष्ठा, ईमानदारी और पूर्ण समर्पण के साथ निभाया है। केंद्रीय शिक्षा मंत्री के रूप में उन्होंने राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति-2020 को प्रभावी रूप से लागू करने में महत्वपूर्ण योगदान दिया। शिक्षा व्यवस्था में अनेक सार्थक... https://t.co/6wUoyXfO8h- Rekha Gupta (@gupta_rekha) July 25, 2026

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday lauded Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation from the Cabinet and his tenure and principled stance, describing his decision to step down as a testament to his dedication to public ethics and national interest.In a post on X, Gupta commended Pradhan's contributions to India's educational landscape, particularly highlighting his role in rolling out key policy frameworks and promoting Indian languages in academia."Honorable Shri @dpradhanbjp Ji has fulfilled every responsibility in his public life with dedication, honesty, and complete devotion. As the Union Education Minister, he made a significant contribution to the effective implementation of the National Education Policy-2020.He advanced numerous meaningful reforms in the education system. Education in Indian languages received a boost, technical and higher education expanded, and new opportunities became available for students. "Addressing the minister's decision to step down, Chief Minister Gupta emphasised that prioritizing national interest over position exemplifies high moral standards in governance."Prioritizing the national interest above all, he has submitted his resignation from his position.This decision reflects his unwavering commitment to ethical values, dignity, and principles in public life. May his continuous efforts in the service of the nation continually reach new heights. Heartfelt best wishes for his bright future."Gupta wished Pradhan success in his future endeavours and said, "May his continuous efforts in the service of the nation continually reach new heights. Heartfelt best wishes for his bright future."Pradhan's resignation came after a month-long agitation at Jantar Mantar led by Cockroach Janata Party and activist Sonam Wangchuk, who sat for a 26-day-long hunger strike as the NEET-UG exam was leaked in May. The re-examination was held on June 21.The momentum peaked on July 20 with CJP's 'Chalo Sansad' march, which was met with police action.Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke, in his first reaction, said, "We have done it. Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned.""Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned. And this resignation is proof that if you people are not afraid, if you people do not bow down to this government, then we can take the resignation of anyone," he added.
Article Summary: Pradhan's resignation came after a month-long agitation at Jantar Mantar led by Cockroach Janata Party and activist Sonam Wangchuk. Gupta commended Pradhan's contributions to India's educational landscape, particularly highlighting his role in rolling out key policy frameworks.

Article Title: 'Serious charges': Court rejects retired judge Giribala Singh's bail plea in Twisha Sharma case
Article Text:
Twisha Sharma death case (File Photo)

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: A special court in Bhopal on Saturday rejected the bail plea of retired judge Giribala Singh, an accused in the alleged dowry death of former model and actor Twisha Sharma, observing that the charges against her were "serious. "Giribala Singh, Twisha's mother-in-law, is accused in the case after the former model and actor was allegedly found hanging at her marital home in Bhopal on May 12.The retired judge and her son, Samarth Singh, were later arrested on charges of dowry-related harassment, mental abuse and domestic violence. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is probing the case.The bail application was initially listed before Special Judge Neelam Shukla, who recused herself from hearing the matter.The case was then transferred to Special Judge Ram Pratap Mishra, who reserved the order on Friday after hearing arguments from both sides.Seeking bail on humanitarian grounds, the defence argued that Singh, an elderly woman with health issues, was not receiving adequate medical care in jail. It also submitted that her nearly 100-year-old mother depended on her for care.The defence further contended that Singh had cooperated with the investigation, suffered a burglary at her residence while in custody, and received a regular salary and a war widow's pension, making the allegation of dowry demand implausible.Opposing the plea, the CBI argued that Singh's gender alone could not justify bail, particularly when the deceased was also a woman. It pointed out that the Madhya Pradesh High Court had on May 27 quashed the anticipatory bail granted to her by a subordinate court in Bhopal.The agency also alleged that Singh had refused to provide her voice sample during the investigation, attempted to influence the probe by contacting a CCTV technician and a salon operator linked to the case, and sent a private representative to obtain CCTV footage.The CBI argued that her release could enable her to influence witnesses, tamper with evidence or hamper the ongoing investigation.After hearing both sides, the special court rejected Singh's bail application.
Article Summary: Giribala Singh, Twisha's mother-in-law, is accused in the case after the former model and actor was allegedly found hanging at her marital home in Bhopal on May 12. Article Title: 'Goons and their future generations will remember': Bengal invokes 'Goonda Act' over NEET protest violence in first use of law
Article Text:
A student protest rally turned violent in Kolkata on Friday (PTI)

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The West Bengal government on Saturday invoked its newly enacted "Goonda Act" against those accused of orchestrating violence during Friday's NEET protest, marking the first use of the legislation since it was passed by the state assembly.The West Bengal Public Safety and Control of Anti-social Activities Act, 2026, was passed by the assembly recently after a stormy debate and criticised by the opposition as draconian.Governor RN Ravi approved the legislation earlier this week.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announced the move on Saturday."I condemn the attack on our journalist friends on behalf of the entire House. An attack on journalists is unacceptable.We will take such action under the Goonda Act that these goons and even their next three generations will remember it. This is precisely why this law was enacted," Adhikari said in the assembly.He informed the House that around 70 people identified from the Dharmatala rally were "not students" and had no connection with the agitation over the NEET paper leak.Seven FIRs were registered over Friday's violence — six at Hare Street police station and one at Entally police station — with provisions of the new law incorporated into the cases, he told the House."The police exercised maximum restraint despite repeated provocation. That was the clear instruction given to them. They did not fall into the trap," Adhikari said.The chief minister alleged that the rally initially proceeded peacefully before "anti-social elements" entered from behind and attempted to trigger violence.According to him, the protest was organised under the banner of the "United Cockroach March", announced by what he described as a self-proclaimed member of the CJP, with participation from Left and ultra-Left student organisations, including the SFI, DSO, DYSA and AISF."In a democracy, everyone has the right to protest peacefully within the framework of law. The police were specifically instructed not to act unless the situation went completely out of control," he added.Adhikari alleged that as the procession reached Dorina Crossing at Esplanade, shoes and water bottles were hurled first at policemen and then at journalists covering the demonstration."They wanted the police to resort to lathi-charge and tear gas. They wanted a spectacle. But Kolkata Police did not provide them that opportunity. The restraint shown by the force deserves appreciation," he stated.
Article Summary: The West Bengal Public Safety and Control of Anti-social Activities Act, 2026, was passed by the assembly recently after a stormy debate.Governor RN Ravi approved the legislation earlier this week. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announced the move on Saturday.

Article Title: Sarnath's ancient Buddhist site now a world heritage site: UNESCO
Article Text:
UNESCO announces new world heritage site in Sarnath

New Delhi: The Ancient Buddhist Site in Sarnath is now a world heritage site. UNESCO inscribed it on the list Saturday during the ongoing 48th session of the world heritage committee in Busan, Korea. With this inscription, India now has 45 World Heritage sites.Tim Curtis, director and representative, UNESCO regional office for south Asia, said: "On behalf of UNESCO, I warmly congratulate govt and the people of India on the inscription of the Ancient Buddhist Site, Sarnath, on the World Heritage List. For more than 2,500 years, Sarnath has been a place of pilgrimage and inspiration for Buddhists around the world.It is here that the Buddha delivered his first sermon, sharing teachings of compassion, wisdom and peace that continue to resonate today. Its temples, stupas, and monasteries bear witness to centuries of faith, devotion, and shared human heritage. Safeguarding this exceptional site is our collective responsibility for present and future generations."Located in Varanasi, one of the world's oldest inhabited cities, the property preserves the architectural and archaeological remains of Sarnath. According to sacred Buddhist texts, the Buddha traveled to Sarnath in the sixth century BCE after attaining enlightenment. It was here that he met his first disciples and delivered his first sermon, an event regarded as the beginning of the spread of Buddhist teachings.
Article Summary: The Ancient Buddhist Site in Sarnath is now a world heritage site. UNESCO inscribed it on the list Saturday during the ongoing 48th session of the world heritage committee in Busan, Korea. It is here that the Buddha delivered his first sermon, sharing teachings of compassion, wisdom and peace that continue to resonate today.

Article Title: Similar symptoms, climate change & testing gaps: Why monsoon illnesses are so often misdiagnosed
Article Text:
Representational image

Impact on newborns

Why the risk is higher among children

Contribution of climate change

Government data reflects rise in malaria cases during the pre-monsoon months

Why diagnosis gets delayed

Nitish Kumar, 22, a student from Nawada, Bihar, first relied on over-the-counter medicines when he began experiencing symptoms of chikungunya in February last year. For almost a week, he believed it was an ordinary viral fever.“I did not immediately go to a doctor. I bought some medicines from a pharmacy to treat the symptoms of what I thought was a viral fever and made some changes to my diet.”Even after seeing a doctor, the mosquito-borne viral disease went undetected. “One day, I noticed a sudden eruption of red spots on my body, and I suspected I was infected with chikungunya. I went to AIIMS Bhopal to see a doctor, but the doctor handed me a list of medicines prescribed for viral fever.Even the doctor could not diagnose it initially despite the rash.”The World Health Organization (WHO) notes that chikungunya symptoms — abrupt fever, swelling, muscle pain, headache, nausea, fatigue — overlap with those of other infections, making misdiagnosis common. If the illness lacks severe joint pain, it may go unnoticed because symptoms in many infected individuals are mild.This is hardly an outlier. The initial symptoms of most monsoon-related illnesses closely overlap with those of common viral fever.“This is a typical situation observed during the rainy season. We come across many cases of patients who present with symptoms such as fever, sore throat, or general body weakness and are treated as viral infections. But after 2 to 3 days, if the high fever persists, body pains, or low platelets indicate influenza or dengue,” said Dr. M. J. Jayakanth, Consultant — Internal Medicine, SPARSH Hospital, Sarjapur Road, Bangalore.For dengue, WHO says most people are asymptomatic, while symptomatic cases experience high fever, headache, body aches, nausea and rash. Malaria’s mild symptoms are similar: fever, chills and headache.The monsoon brings relief from summer heat, especially in northern India, but also a hidden cost: a surge of infections. Pools of stagnant water left by heavy downpours become mosquito breeding grounds, fueling spread of vector-borne illnesses like malaria, dengue and chikungunya. Heavy rainfall and high humidity also allow airborne viruses, including influenza, to linger longer, and as people retreat indoors, close contact in poorly ventilated spaces facilitates transmission. Because many monsoon illnesses begin with fever and headache — symptoms associated with viral fever — delayed detection can allow them to worsen into life-threatening conditions.Dr Manish Mittal, senior consultant paediatrician at Cocoon Hospital in Jaipur, says newborns and toddlers are more vulnerable during the monsoon because of immature immune systems. “The combination of high humidity, pollution through dirty water, a moist environment, and mosquitoes increases their susceptibility to lung infections, diarrhoea, skin infections, and vector-borne diseases. Even a small infection may develop into something serious in infants. ”Delayed detection is common in children because they cannot always communicate symptoms clearly. “Parents sometimes seek medical care only after dehydration, persistent fever, or unusual lethargy develops, which can delay timely diagnosis and treatment.”Dr. Mittal recommends parents ensure hygiene at home: keep surroundings dry, use clean water, protect babies from mosquitoes, and continue breastfeeding if feasible. “If the infant has fever, poor feeding, lethargy, vomiting, diarrhoea, low urine output, or difficulty breathing, prompt medical care is required.”On the UNDP blog, Kathryn Johnson, a policy specialist in HIV and health for the UNDP regional office for Asia-Pacific, writes that changing rainfall patterns and rising temperatures increase the risk of vector-borne diseases in rapidly urbanising regions with weak health infrastructure. “Warmer climates extend the breeding seasons and geographical range of many vectors, while increased rainfall or poor water management in urban settings provides ideal conditions for their spread. ”This complicates diagnosis, as these diseases are no longer confined to the monsoon season.Abhay Tripathi, 22, a journalism student at Central University of Odisha, says he contracted chikungunya last May in Bhopal, a month of high temperatures. Because it wasn’t monsoon, he assumed it was ordinary fever. “I did not go to the doctor on the first day because, being a student living away from home, I thought it was just a fever. I took a paracetamol that I had in my room and rested for a day. But on the second day, the fever didn't break, and I noticed minor rashes on my hand. I got worried and decided to see a doctor.”Government data show rising malaria cases in pre- and post-monsoon months. The National Centre for Vector-Borne Disease Control’s monthly report records a slight rise in positive malaria cases in 2025 during pre-monsoon months compared with 2024. Mapped against the three-year average, the increase is significant, especially in months approaching peak summer.Dr. Jayakanth says climate change is not the sole contributor. Improved testing and surveillance have picked up cases that earlier went unreported. “Urban water storage, construction sites, poor drainage, and changing human movement patterns also create year-round breeding habitats.”“So, this trend is probably not due to a single factor; it reflects a combination of climate change, environmental changes, urbanisation, and better disease detection systems,” he adds.Gaps remain in diagnostic infrastructure and mechanisms, including low availability of rapid diagnostic tests in peripheral areas, delays in laboratory results, poor early screening, and limited healthcare infrastructure in both urban and rural areas. “Most primary hospitals do not have the infrastructure to conduct tests on-site, meaning that the samples will be taken to external laboratories, hence causing a delay,” he says.Ultimately, this escalating public health challenge is more than a seasonal inconvenience. Climate change is reshaping environmental patterns and vector habitats, while access to advanced diagnostics remains unequal — a convergence that is intensifying the risk and reach of these illnesses.
Article Summary: The monsoon brings relief from summer heat, especially in northern India, but also a hidden cost: a surge of infections. Pools of stagnant water left by heavy downpours become mosquito breeding grounds, fueling spread of vector-borne illnesses. Heavy rainfall and high humidity also allow airborne viruses, including influenza, to linger longer.
